_comment: The four adventurers' own conversations. Written by residents_talk_export.py from drafting/residents_answers_approved.json: edit that. rank: the lowest rank that hears the answer; lock: the reply below it; says version 'opened:<quest>': the answer once that quest is completed, at any rank.

AGHallResidentOrc: Ghrulek, a warrior out of Largashbur in the Rift! The Guild calls me C-rank, and I earned it one job at a time. Why do I live here?
Because nobody in Skyrim cooks like Henriette!
The Code of Malacath. A grown son challenges the chief, or he leaves. Shagrol was a good chief, and I would not raise my axe against him.
So I left, as young Orcs do, to make my own name. If I go back, I must fight whoever sits in his place. This hall is my clan now.

nodes.prompt: What kind of work do you take?

AGHallResidentOrc: Warrior's work. Giants, bandit chiefs, anything too big for the others to take. Give me a fight that comes straight at me. No tricks, no hiding.
Dead. Yamarz killed him in combat and took Largashbur, or so the story goes. I'm not sure how a weakling like Yamarz could do such a thing though.
opened:DA06: You've been to Largashbur, so you know the rest. Heard Yamarz is dead, Malacath's curse is lifted, and Gularzob leads them now.
You're a brother to me for doing that.

AGHallResidentOrc: That's a story for someone who's been through more than you. Come back with a few more kills behind you.

AGHallResidentRanger: Not much to say. Pale-born and raised to hunt. I take work others won't, and I take it because it pays.
My mother. She had me tracking wolves and other prey before I was twelve.
She's dead. A legendary sabre cat tore her apart, out in the wilds. My father raised me after.

nodes.prompt: Why the Guild, and not something like a guard?

AGHallResidentRanger: Guards stand where they're told for a pittance. The Guild pays by the job, and I pick the jobs. I took this path because I hunt for myself.

nodes.prompt: Have you ever gone after it?

AGHallResidentRanger: Once or twice. I know its trail and no one has collected the bounty on it yet. When the time's right, I'll claim it. For the coin.
That's none of your business with such a low rank.

nodes.prompt: You don't talk about the guild like the others here.

AGHallResidentRanger: Why, because I treat a job like an actual job? That's all this guild is.
The sooner you learn that heroics and glory are for the dead and good coin is for the living the better.

AGHallResidentScout: This one came out of Elsweyr with a caravan of his own once. Now he walks Skyrim scouting for the Guild.
A good nose, a good memory, and every road in Skyrim. That is Zhasim.
For years, this one's little caravan walked every pass in Skyrim. Then bandits came down from the rocks and broke it apart.
Still, he learned every road doing it, so it was not all bad. Mostly bad. But not all.

nodes.prompt: How do you find these places?

AGHallResidentScout: Khajiit follows his nose, the wind and the drunk talk of hunters. A path too worn for goats, smoke where no farm stands. Something is always there.
Then he sells it to Merila, and it goes on her map.
Most things, this one could buy again. Not the claw. An iron claw, his ancestor's, carried in a war long ago and handed down to him.
The bandits took it, and he has not seen it since.
Not yet, friend. Walk a few more roads for the Guild, and I will tell it.

AGHallResidentVeteran: Old soldier, old adventurer, A-rank by the end. I came north to help start this hall. When the Legion called the company up, I was its sergeant.
Brought home what I could. Now I sit in the attic and correct everyone's footwork.

nodes.prompt: Where did you learn to fight?

AGHallResidentVeteran: In the Legion, same as most. I earned respect and honor there and lost it all by running my mouth to the wrong commander.
I walked out in disgrace, but the Guild still took me in. Best trade I ever made.
Mud and waiting, mostly. Then the fighting, and I'd sooner not talk about it. Ask me something else.

nodes.prompt: An old A-rank, sleeping in the attic?

AGHallResidentVeteran: And where should I sleep? Some cottage by a river, waiting to die? This hall's the only home I've had since the war.
I moved in the day it reopened, and I'd like to see someone try to move me out.

nodes.prompt: What did you say to him?

AGHallResidentVeteran: I told him, to his face and in front of his soldiers, that his order would get them killed. I was right and it did. They all died for nothing.
The indignant bastard had me blamed for his failure instead.
That's not a story for green ears. Come back when you've seen a few things.
